claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructure.
A framework combining microstructural descriptors, machine learning, and reduced-order physics simulation can predict the tensile and fracture properties of HfNbTiVAl10.
The combined framework can predict Young’s modulus more accurately and rapidly than established simulation approaches.
The combined framework can predict yield strength more accurately and rapidly than established simulation approaches.
The combined framework can predict fracture toughness more accurately and rapidly than established simulation approaches.
Phase distribution, grain-size gradients, and interphase boundaries are informative microstructure-derived features for the proposed model.
The hierarchical heterostructure provides spatially varying phase and grain architecture.
The spatially varying phase and grain architecture mediates load transfer during deformation.
The spatially varying phase and grain architecture mediates stress distribution during deformation.
Correlations between high-resolution microstructural descriptors and mechanical performance can be learned to map microstructural signatures to mechanical-response parameters.
Rapid inference from the trained model can substitute for full-scale simulation and thereby reduce computational complexity.
The proposed model will achieve prediction errors of no more than 10% for Young’s modulus.
The proposed model will achieve prediction errors of no more than 10% for yield strength.
The proposed model will achieve prediction errors of no more than 10% for fracture toughness.
The proposed model will reduce computational time by approximately a factor of three relative to established finite-element or continuum simulations.
Large deviations between tested microstructures and the training distribution may cause the approach to fail.
Unexpected phase interactions may cause the approach to fail.
The approach may fail when hierarchical structure does not dominate deformation under the tested conditions.
Failure to achieve predictions consistently within ±10% while also failing to obtain a threefold time reduction would falsify the hypothesis.
Independent evidence of strong decoupling between the selected microstructural features and mechanical behavior would falsify the hypothesis.
